items: A calmer screen: a chosen option now has a quiet grey outline. Orange is kept for the main button of each step, the camera and the time counter.
A bigger picture: in the Frame and Export steps the left panel folds to a thin strip. Click the strip, or go back to Build, to open it again.
The camera panel has three tabs: Shot, Move and Lens. The aspect ratio and the guides now sit above the picture.
Starter sets show a picture of each set and open on a clear view of the scene. An empty stage tells you how to begin.
Clearer messages, at the top of the view: a green tick when something finished, a red edge when something needs you. Tooltips appear at once.
Exporting a video ends on a "Video saved" window with the file name and where it was saved.
One File menu, at the top of the window, with Recent projects and Export. ShotRef remembers the size and place of its window.
See before you click: hover a camera move, a motion feel, a lens, a shot size or a pose, and a small moving preview shows what it will do to your shot.
The Items list sorts your scene into groups (People, Vehicles, Buildings, Furniture and more). Click a group's name to fold it, or use its eye to hide the whole group.
Double-click an item's name in the Items list to rename it.
A calmer, clearer look: each section sits on its own card with a clear heading, and a chosen option always has the same orange outline.
Less on screen: panels show what you use most, and rarely used sections start folded. Nothing was removed: every control is still there.
Scene presets, clouds and "Light the shot from" are now picture tiles, so you can see the look before you pick it.
Shorter labels, with one name for each thing (for example "Aim camera at this" and "Clear move").
Skies with clouds: pick the cover, the look and how fast they drift. Clouds soften the sun and are named in the prompt.
Drag people and props from the Add panel straight onto the view.
After an update, this box lists what changed since the version you had.
ShotRef's messages (updates, About, file errors) now look like ShotRef and open without the Windows alert sound.
A quick tour of the screen: orange viewfinder corners frame each part, with a line or two on each. It changes nothing in your scene.
Take the tour again any time from the Help menu or the top of the Quick start page.
Editor, Top and Camera (and split view) moved into a View group in the row under the picture, so the top bar is cleaner.
The Windows app updates itself: it checks for a new version shortly after launch and asks before downloading or restarting.
Help, Check for updates checks on demand. Help, Check for updates automatically turns the launch check off.
